content: Ribavirin is not effective in treating hepatitis C unless it is used in combination with another medication. If you have hepatitis C, your doctor will prescribe an additional medication to take alongside ribavirin. It is essential to take both medications exactly as instructed by your healthcare provider. Ribavirin can cause anemia, a condition characterized by a reduction in red blood cells. Additionally, notify your doctor if you have or have had heart disease. If you experience symptoms such as extreme fatigue, pale skin, headache, dizziness, confusion, rapid heartbeat, weakness, shortness of breath, or chest pain, contact your doctor immediately. It is crucial to attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor and undergo regular laboratory tests. Blood tests will be conducted before starting ribavirin and frequently during the first four weeks of treatment. Your doctor or pharmacist will provide you with a Medication Guide from the manufacturer when you begin treatment and each time you refill your prescription. Read this information carefully and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. You can also access the Medication Guide on the FDA website. Discuss the risks of taking ribavirin with your doctor. For female patients: Do not take ribavirin if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. A pregnancy test must confirm that you are not pregnant before starting ribavirin. You must use two forms of birth control and undergo monthly pregnancy tests during treatment and for six months after completing treatment. If you become pregnant during this time, contact your doctor immediately. Ribavirin can cause severe harm or death to the fetus. For male patients: Do not take ribavirin if your partner is pregnant or planning to become pregnant. You must use two forms of birth control, including a condom with spermicide, during treatment and for six months afterward. Your partner must undergo monthly pregnancy tests during this period. If your partner becomes pregnant, contact your doctor immediately. Ribavirin can cause severe harm or death to the fetus. Ribavirin is used in combination with another medication, typically an interferon, to treat hepatitis C. It belongs to a class of antiviral drugs known as nucleoside analogues. Ribavirin works by inhibiting the replication of the hepatitis C virus within the body. However, it is not yet known whether treatment with ribavirin and another medication can cure hepatitis C, prevent liver damage caused by the virus, or stop the spread of hepatitis C to others. Ribavirin is available as tablets, capsules, and an oral solution. It is usually taken twice daily, in the morning and evening, for a duration of 24 to 48 weeks or longer. Ribavirin tablets should be taken with food. Capsules and oral solutions should also be taken with food unless your doctor advises otherwise. It is best to take ribavirin at the same times each day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Do not take more or less of the medication or take it more frequently than prescribed. Shake the oral solution well before use and wash the measuring device after each use. If side effects occur, your doctor may adjust your dose or temporarily stop the medication. Do not alter your dose or stop taking ribavirin without your doctor’s approval. Ribavirin is sometimes used to treat viral hemorrhagic fevers, which are severe viral infections that can cause internal and external bleeding, organ failure, and death. In cases of biological warfare, ribavirin may be used to treat deliberately spread viral hemorrhagic fevers. It is also occasionally used to treat severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS), a viral illness that can cause respiratory distress, pneumonia, and death. Discuss the potential risks of using ribavirin for these conditions with your doctor. Before taking ribavirin, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to ribavirin or any other medications. If you are taking ribavirin tablets, notify your doctor if you are allergic to corn. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Mention any medications for anxiety, depression, mental illness, HIV/AIDS, or immune suppression, as well as any antacids if you are taking ribavirin capsules. Your doctor may need to adjust your medications or monitor you for side effects. Inform your doctor if you consume large amounts of alcohol, use or have used street drugs, or have ever had suicidal thoughts or attempts. Additionally, disclose any history of organ transplants, mental illness, cancer, psoriasis, HIV/AIDS, diabetes, sarcoidosis, Gilbert’s syndrome, gout, liver disease (other than hepatitis C), or thyroid, kidney, pancreas, eye, or lung conditions. Do not breastfeed while taking ribavirin. Ribavirin may cause drowsiness, dizziness, or confusion. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how the medication affects you. Do not consume alcohol while taking ribavirin, as it can worsen liver disease. Drink plenty of fluids while taking ribavirin. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If you do not remember until the next day, contact your doctor for instructions. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Mild side effects of ribavirin include cough, upset stomach, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, heartburn, loss of appetite, weight loss, changes in taste, dry mouth, difficulty concentrating, trouble sleeping, memory loss, rash, dry or itchy skin, sweating, irregular menstruation, muscle or bone pain, and hair loss. Inform your doctor if these symptoms persist or worsen. Severe side effects are rare but require immediate medical attention. These include hives, swelling of the face or extremities, hoarseness, difficulty swallowing or breathing, severe stomach or back pain, bloody or black stools, unusual bleeding or bruising, vision changes, signs of infection, depression, suicidal thoughts, mood changes, excessive worry, irritability, substance abuse relapse, worsening psoriasis, or intolerance to cold. Ribavirin may also slow growth and weight gain in children. Report any unusual symptoms to your doctor. Store ribavirin tablets and capsules at room temperature, away from heat and moisture. Store the oral solution in the refrigerator or at room temperature. Keep the medication out of reach of children and dispose of expired or unused medication properly. In case of overdose, contact a poison control center or emergency services immediately. Do not share ribavirin with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
